summary: The new version's Django migration creates a B-tree index on account_user.last_name using CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, which executes non-blockingly without row modifications. deploy_new runs this migration (migration: 'apply') and starts the new version. retire_old follows after smoke checks. No SQL stages are required because the index creation is concurrent and preserves existing last_name values; the old version's model includes last_name, preventing Django save() from overwriting it with NULL.
write_consistency: During the overlap, the old version's saves include last_name (its model knows the column), so values are not lost. The new version's index build via CONCURRENTLY does not rewrite rows, keeping pre-existing last_name values intact. Both versions read/write the same rows interleaved, and the note column checks pass as no data mutations occur beyond the index creation.

stages.description: Retire the old Saleor version; after this stage only the new version handles traffic.
